THE COMPLETELY IMPARTIAL REPORT

The best app for learning Japanese.
According to the fish who works there.

Kanji, grammar, the JLPT and the quiet thrill of becoming the person who says, “Wait, I can read that.”

Presented by DoDon · Words: Kanjidon Team
7 minutes of extremely serious fish propaganda

OPEN PACKS. COLLECT. REMEMBER. The method is serious. The speaker has fins.
Your motiveThe evidenceMission JLPTThe verdict

You know that moment when someone points at some Japanese writing and you say: “Wait. I can read that.”

The room goes silent. A violin starts playing by itself. Your friend who “only watches anime in the original Japanese” suddenly stops chewing.

That. That’s the moment we work for. Even if nobody actually claps and the sign just says “exit”. You still read it. No camera. No summoning Google. Just your very respectable brain.

I’m DoDon. I have fins, a light bulb on my head and an outrageously high opinion of Kanjidon: the app where kanji become cards you unpack, quizzes put you to the test and review gives your memory another chance. Then come grammar, reading and the JLPT. Yes, there’s a syllabus behind this face.

01 / EVERY GREAT UNDERTAKING NEEDS A MOTIVE

Why do you want to learn Japanese?
We accept less noble answers too.

An exam, a trip, a manga. Or the unstoppable desire to be the clever one in your group. No judgment. I’m opening a case file.

A

You’re starting from scratch.

Right now, “I know Japanese” means you recognise the word sushi. Excellent. We’ve established a starting point.

Start with hiragana and katakana, then build your foundations with kanji, vocabulary and grammar. You don’t have to arrive prepared to earn the right to begin.

Open the beginner’s case file ↗
B

You want to pass the JLPT.

Your idea of adrenaline is a timer next to a question in Japanese. Respect. Mild concern, but respect.

Materials for N5 through N1 and mock exams give your review a concrete goal. The certificate doesn’t come out of a card pack. Preparation, however, is something you build.

Call the war council ↗
C

You want to be the coolest friend.

Someone shows you a sign. Everyone else opens their camera. You take that unbearably elegant pause before reading it aloud.

Quizzes and review train what you actually remember. The real flex isn’t a huge collection. It’s using what you’ve learned. Applause from friends remains optional.

D

You’re already advanced.

You’ve moved past “what a pretty symbol”. Now you notice grammatical nuances and have complicated feelings about a reading you forgot.

Advanced kanji, vocabulary and content let you keep going deeper. Knowing a lot doesn’t make review illegal. I checked.

02 / NICE JOKE. NOW SHOW US THE EVIDENCE.

A pack sparks your curiosity.
A quiz makes you think.

Opening a pack and discovering a card is fun. But the card can’t sit an exam for you. It has other commitments. Being rectangular, for example.

That’s why Kanjidon pairs collecting with quizzes and spaced repetition: you recall meanings and readings, make mistakes, try again and meet the content again during review.

You feel the difference when you move from “this kanji looks familiar” to “I know what it means”. One is learning. The other is your brain waving at an acquaintance in the supermarket.

01. Open a pack

Curiosity opens the door.

02. Test yourself

03. Come back to review

ENOUGH SLIDES. PHONES OUT.

It’s a real app.
The fish didn’t draw the buttons.

Here’s Kanjidon in action: open a pack, take a quiz, build your foundations. The “yes, but show me” department may take a seat.

03 / GETTING STARTED WITHOUT SUMMONING PANIC

Japanese from zero.
No entrance exam for curious minds.

If a page of Japanese looks like an elegant blackout, this is a good place to begin. Start with kana, get familiar with the sounds and add one piece at a time.

Kanjidon also has grammar lessons and reading material: recognising a word is great, but knowing what it’s doing inside a sentence is even better. Like knowing the guests, then discovering whose wedding it is.

THE FIVE-YEAR PLAN YOU CAN FINISH BEFORE COFFEE

Today’s agenda: one small topic, a few questions, some review. Done. No retreat on Mount Fuji, no €47 notebook, no transformation into someone who wakes up at five. The board has also approved pyjamas.

04 / FOR PEOPLE WHOSE GOAL HAS AN ACRONYM

Prepare for the JLPT.
With fewer lucky rituals.

Whether you’re aiming for N5 or tackling the advanced levels, Kanjidon gives you a place to practise kanji, vocabulary and grammar, and test yourself with mock exams.

Use them to identify what you don’t know yet, then revisit it methodically. A wrong answer is something to work on. Not a ruling from the Supreme Court of Kanji.

And yes: you still need regular study, listening and reading practice, and practice beyond the app. Kanjidon helps you prepare. It doesn’t sign off on a pass. My fin isn’t licensed.

05 / TABLE APPROVED BY THE COMMITTEE OF FINS

Tell me your goal.
I’ll tell you where to start.

Your planWhat to use in KanjidonWhat matters
“I’m starting from zero”Kana, first kanji, grammarBuild your foundations, step by step.

06 / SECONDARY MOTIVES, STILL APPROVED

It’s fine if you just want to
understand that menu.

Or read a manga without stopping at every panel. Recognise more words in a song. Prepare for a trip. Return to Japanese after a break lasting “a few weeks”, according to the geological definition of a week.

You don’t need a prestigious reason. You need your own reason. Cards give you something to discover, missions and leagues add a challenge, and studying gives the whole thing substance.

“Your dream might be reading a novel.
It might also be ordering dinner with dignity.
I support both departments.”DoDon, head of ambitions and side dishes

And when you’re already good? Keep reading, listening and speaking in the real world. Use Kanjidon to keep your knowledge active and tackle new things. The goal isn’t to become brilliant at using an app. It’s to do more in Japanese.

RAISE YOUR FIN IF YOU HAVE A QUESTION

“Nice fish.
But what about me?”

Questions collected before the speaker awards himself another degree.

I only know “sushi”. Can I come in?

Come on in. There’s no bouncer testing your kanji. Start with hiragana and katakana, then add vocabulary and grammar. Zero is a perfectly respectable starting point. Minus one would be awkward anyway.

I’m advanced. Will I spend six months relearning “hello”?

Your learning career doesn’t have to restart with greetings. Materials go up to N1: explore advanced content and review the shaky bits. Even experts have that kanji they recognise perfectly, provided someone supplies the answer.

Cute cards. Is there actual studying underneath?

Caught red-handed. There are quizzes, spaced repetition, grammar, reading and JLPT mock exams. The cards catch your attention; then your brain has to take part. It had hoped to turn up just for the buffet.

So I download Kanjidon and the JLPT surrenders?

That would be convenient. I sent the proposal. No reply. Kanjidon helps you prepare and work out what to review; results take study and practice. We bring the tools. You bring that lovely thing called consistency. The fish cheers you on.

Can I study without wanting to take an exam?

Of course. Manga, travel, songs, curiosity or reading a sign without help: your reason is enough. No motivation letter required. I’m here because they needed a fish.

THE FINAL, COINCIDENTALLY FAVOURABLE VERDICT

Japanese takes effort.
Boredom is optional.

If you want a Japanese learning app that combines studying with a reason to come back, Kanjidon has plenty going for it. And a mascot willing to explain every reason, uninvited.

Start at your level. Discover a card. Try a quiz.
Then come back for what you want to remember.

Open packs. Collect. Remember.
Report concluded. You may clap your fins.
